html:
Italy became a single state in 1861, when the Kingdom of Sardinia, ruled from Turin by the House of Savoy, joined most of the peninsula under King Victor Emmanuel II. Venice was added in 1866 and Rome in 1870, which then became the capital.

Since the fall of the western Roman Empire, Italy had been divided: city states such as Venice, Florence and Genoa, the Papal States, the Kingdom of Naples, and lands ruled by Spain and Austria. Napoleon briefly joined much of it into French run states, and the idea of a nation took hold.

How unification happened, the Risorgimento:

  • Revolts in 1848 failed.
  • Cavour, prime minister of Sardinia, won French help to beat Austria in 1859 and take Lombardy.
  • In 1860 Garibaldi and his thousand red shirted volunteers conquered Sicily and Naples and handed them to the king.
  • Venice came after Prussia beat Austria in 1866; Rome after French troops left in 1870. The Pope refused to accept it.

The new state was poor and split between a richer north and a poorer south, and millions emigrated, many to the Americas. Italy joined the Allies in the First World War. In 1922 Mussolini took power and built the first fascist state. He allied with Hitler's Germany in the Second World War, and Italy was invaded and defeated.

In 1946 Italians voted to end the monarchy. The Republic grew fast in the 1950s and 1960s and was a founding member of what became the European Union.
sum: Italy became a single state in 1861, when the Kingdom of Sardinia, ruled from Turin by the House of Savoy, joined most of the peninsula under King Victor Emmanuel II. Venice was added in 1866 and Rome in 1870, which then became the capital.
